_about: Basics writer (learn/ pages). General ML and KV-cache terms. Search all glossary files before you add a term; do not redefine these ids.

llm.short: Large language model. A neural network that reads tokens and predicts the next token, one token at a time.

token.short: The unit of text that a model reads and writes: a word, a part of a word, or a symbol. The model sees each token as an integer id.

attention.short: The layer step where each token looks at the earlier tokens. It compares its query with their keys and makes a weighted sum of their values.

query-key-value.short: Three vectors that attention makes for each token. The query asks, the keys of earlier tokens answer, and the values carry the content that is mixed.

attention-head.short: One independent copy of attention inside a layer. A layer has several heads; each head has its own queries, keys and values of size head_dim.

prefill.short: The first phase of generation. The model reads all prompt tokens in one pass and fills the KV cache for them.

decode.short: The second phase of generation. Each step makes one new token per sequence (more with speculative decoding) and adds its keys and values to the KV cache.

kv-cache.short: Device memory that keeps the keys and values of earlier tokens, so that each new token does not compute them again.
kv-cache.long: In DeepInfer the main cache is paged in blocks of 128 tokens ({{cite deepinfer/model_executor/model_metadata_utils.py:133-135}}). Each sequence also has one state slot with its sliding-window cache.

kv-block.short: A fixed-size part of the KV cache that holds the keys and values of a fixed number of tokens. In DeepInfer one block holds 128 tokens for all layers.
kv-block.long: Block 0 is never given to a sequence; the free list starts at block 1 ({{cite csrc/engine/block_manager.hpp:27-35}}).

block-table.short: A list per sequence that maps its logical block 0, 1, 2 ... to physical block ids in the KV cache pool.
block-table.long: In DeepInfer it is std::vector<int> block_table in KvCacheState ({{cite csrc/engine/sequence.hpp:200-207}}).

paged-kv-cache.short: A KV cache that is split into fixed-size blocks. A sequence gets blocks one at a time, from anywhere in the pool, and a block table records where they are.

fragmentation.short: Memory that is reserved but not used. With paging, only the last block of each sequence can be partly empty (internal fragmentation).

preemption.short: The scheduler takes the KV blocks away from a running sequence because the pool is full. The sequence stops, or waits and is computed again later.

sequence.short: The engine object for one request: its tokens, its state (waiting, running, finished) and its KV cache blocks.

block-manager.short: The C++ object that owns the free list of KV cache blocks. It gives blocks to sequences and takes them back.
block-manager.long: Defined in {{cite csrc/engine/block_manager.hpp:119-187}}. DeepInfer makes two: one for KV blocks and one for state slots.

state-slot.short: A fixed-size area of device memory per running sequence in DeepInfer. It holds the sliding-window cache and the compression state of that sequence.
state-slot.long: The C++ field is state_id ({{cite csrc/engine/sequence.hpp:207}}); the layout is StateBlock ({{cite deepinfer/worker/cache_engine.py:221-241}}).

sliding-window-attention.short: Attention that looks only at the most recent W tokens (the window), not at all earlier tokens. Its cache has a fixed size per sequence.

kv-compression.short: Storing one cache entry for every n tokens instead of one per token. DeepInfer supports the ratios 1 and 2 (C1, C2).

memory-profiling.short: A test forward pass at start-up. It measures the peak device memory of the model, so that the engine knows how much memory is left for the KV cache.
